TH9VCN6UkyQ.summary: Jonathan Blow's first talk on designing a new programming language for games, which became Jai. He explains the problems with C++ and why Go, Rust and D do not fit game development.
TH9VCN6UkyQ.why: HN programmers recommend it, and the Jai series that followed, for the game-industry view on replacing C++ and for watching a language being invented.

T647CGsuOVU.summary: The first part of Welch Labs' series on imaginary numbers, presenting them as the natural extension of the number line into two dimensions. It covers the history and the math with strong visuals.
T647CGsuOVU.why: HN commenters rate the series as some of the best visual teaching on complex numbers and recommend it for building intuition.

Tb823aqgX_0.summary: Mark Bastian contrasts top-down object-oriented design with bottom-up, data-oriented design in Clojure. He models a board game as plain data plus small composable functions and compares it with a roughly 22-class OOP version.
Tb823aqgX_0.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the talk that made data-oriented, REPL-driven bottom-up design click.

TfYf_rPWUdY.summary: A short animation from the DNA Learning Center showing how mRNA carries a gene's message to the ribosome, where tRNA and codons are used to assemble amino acids into a protein.
TfYf_rPWUdY.why: Frequently linked as a mind-blowing visualization of how RNA is translated into protein, especially in threads on mRNA vaccines and cell biology.

T71ibcZAX3I.summary: Author JL Collins discusses his book The Simple Path to Wealth at Google, covering avoiding debt, simple index fund investing, and retirement accounts like 401(k)s and IRAs. It is an hour-long interview in plain language.
T71ibcZAX3I.why: HN points people to it as the clearest single video on simple, long-term index fund investing.

T0CpOYZZZW4.summary: Jenny Nicholson's roughly four-hour review of her two-night stay on Disney's Star Wars Galactic Starcruiser immersive hotel. She goes through the experience, its story and production, and why it failed.
T0CpOYZZZW4.why: HN people strongly recommend it as the best overview of the Galactic Starcruiser and a case study in misaligned incentives and poor guest experience, engaging despite its length.

TgmA48fILq8.summary: Bryan Cantrill's 2007 Google Tech Talk on DTrace, showing how dynamic tracing improves debugging of both development and live production systems. It includes a vivid war story about tracking down a problem on a Sun Ray server.
TgmA48fILq8.why: HN regards it as a gem of a technical talk that tackles a fundamental debugging problem and shows a new technology solving it.

Tv6aJRGpz_A.summary: A documentary by Stuart Brown (XboxAhoy) on the history of first-person shooters on the Amiga and how Doom's arrival affected the platform.
Tv6aJRGpz_A.why: Recommended as a well-researched piece of computing history on Amiga FPS games and Doom's impact.

TTFoJQSd48c.summary: Daniel Dennett's Royal Institution lecture on whether the brain is a computer and where its software comes from. He argues that minds are built by evolution and culture, with competence arising without comprehension.
TTFoJQSd48c.why: Cited as an excellent entry point to Dennett's thinking on minds, memes and competence without comprehension.

TlLIOgWYVpI.summary: Herbert Wolverson's Roguelike Celebration 2020 talk surveying procedural map generation techniques, including integration of hand-crafted prefabs and vaults.
TlLIOgWYVpI.why: HN recommends it as a fun, informative survey of easy-to-implement dungeon generation methods from the author of the Rust roguelike tutorial.

T3u7bGgVspM.summary: Devine Lu Linvega of Hundred Rabbits talks about low-power, offline computing, esoteric languages and the Uxn virtual machine, informed by years of sailing the Pacific. The talk frames computing sustainability through a permaculture lens.
T3u7bGgVspM.why: Praised as a standout, non-standard Strange Loop talk explaining the reasoning behind Uxn and resilient computing.

T2OxO-4YLRk.summary: Timothy Cain's 2012 GDC postmortem of the original Fallout, covering how he helped build the game and set the template for open-world RPGs. He talks through production, design and programming decisions.
T2OxO-4YLRk.why: Held up as an exemplary GDC postmortem and a first-hand account for fans of the original Fallout.

T42WuUpBuHE.summary: A recording from real hardware of Tim Follin's multichannel 1-bit music for Agent X on the ZX Spectrum. It shows several voices coaxed out of the single-bit beeper.
T42WuUpBuHE.why: Cited as the prime example of what clever programming can do with a 1-bit audio output.

T5RmMNDR5XI.summary: Elasticsearch engineer and Lucene committer Adrien Grand explains the design decisions inside a Lucene index and what problems it can and cannot solve. The talk goes into how Lucene stores data for fast search and analytics.
T5RmMNDR5XI.why: HN recommends it as an instructive, easy-to-follow look at Lucene internals from a core committer.

T6X2uwlQGQM.summary: Chai Jing's 104-minute documentary on China's smog, with full English subtitles. A former TV anchor, she investigates what smog is, where it comes from and what can be done, prompted by her daughter's health problems.
T6X2uwlQGQM.why: Recommended as an accessible, powerful introduction to severe urban air pollution, remembered also for being banned in China.

TPpoJGYlW54.summary: A Vox explainer on how the wildlife trade and wet markets are linked to coronavirus and why new diseases keep emerging in China. It stresses that most people in China do not eat wildlife.
TPpoJGYlW54.why: HN commenters shared it during early 2020 as a clear explanation of wet markets and how human encroachment on wildlife drives outbreaks.

TVgQ_tgWMyU.summary: Clinical psychologist Dr Michael Yapko draws on forty years of practice and research to explain skills that help people recover from, and even prevent, depression. He emphasizes cognitive and social factors beyond medication.
TVgQ_tgWMyU.why: HN commenters recommend it as a comprehensive talk on depression, and one says it helped them through a bad period.

TVwKjGbz60k.summary: A short excerpt from The Pervert's Guide to Ideology in which Slavoj Zizek analyzes John Carpenter's They Live. He uses the film's fight scene and sunglasses to explain how ideology works.
TVwKjGbz60k.why: HN cites it as a concise, memorable explanation of ideology, often in threads about advertising, propaganda or AI-shaped narratives.

TruCIPy79w8.summary: Milton Friedman explains why the US tax code is enormously complex and why meaningful reform is unlikely. He argues that politicians profit from the complexity, since tax breaks are products they sell and the code works as a tool of reward and punishment. The clip is about 14 minutes from his lecture series.
TruCIPy79w8.why: HN commenters cite it whenever a thread touches on tax complexity, loopholes, or why companies like Intuit benefit from a convoluted tax system.

TwKpj2ISQAc.summary: Physicist Angela Collier's nearly three-hour critique of Richard Feynman's public legacy. She examines how his books, written with Ralph Leighton, shaped a mythologized great-man image, and covers his personal behavior.
TwKpj2ISQAc.why: HN recommends it as a sobering counterpoint to the Feynman myth for people whose view comes from Surely You're Joking.

TwRjO3kHxU4.summary: The Tokyo Llama channel details how the creators found and bought an abandoned akiya minka house in Japan. It covers process, costs, taxes, financing and risks of renovation.
TwRjO3kHxU4.why: Recommended as a candid look at the real costs and paperwork of buying and renovating an abandoned Japanese home.

TPg4Vcr56F0.summary: A Pitchfork TV documentary following Dan Deacon in Montana as he finishes his album Bromst. It shows the experimentation behind it, including pieces written for MIDI-driven player pianos.
TPg4Vcr56F0.why: HN points to it in threads on black MIDI and player pianos as a look at an artist writing tuneful music beyond human playability.

TQB0KK2rxcw.summary: Dan Holohan, author of The Lost Art of Steam Heating, talks about the old steam heating systems he learned about from veteran tradesmen. He shares stories and practical lessons on how these systems work, including running steam at low temperatures.
TQB0KK2rxcw.why: HN recommends it as an informative talk on steam heating whose advice to respect old working systems carries over to software.

TQMbvJNRpLE.summary: Stephen Duneier describes a decision-making approach that took him from struggling with simple tasks to achieving ambitious goals. The talk centers on breaking goals into small marginal adjustments.
TQMbvJNRpLE.why: HN people recommend it for its simple, powerful idea of marginal adjustments and its usefulness for tackling big projects.

Td_PGkfIdIQ.summary: Gabe Newell of Valve speaks at UT Austin's LBJ School on productivity, economics, political institutions and the future of corporations. He discusses in-game economies and how Valve organizes work.
Td_PGkfIdIQ.why: Pointed to as an in-depth view of how Valve is run and how Newell thinks about workers, management and customers.

Tdj8gh9GPc4.summary: A 1995 episode of The Computer Chronicles devoted to Gary Kildall, creator of CP/M. It works as a retrospective and tribute to the personal computer pioneer.
Tdj8gh9GPc4.why: HN recommends it to see what Kildall was like in real life and as a tribute to an influential figure.

Tfh0ytz8S0k.summary: The 8-Bit Guy explains the color limitations of 1980s computers and consoles such as the NES and Commodore 64. It shows how sprites, attributes and palettes shaped the look of old games.
Tfh0ytz8S0k.why: Recommended as a clear, approachable explanation of how retro graphics hardware actually worked.

TqKQ94DtS54.summary: An Isaac Arthur episode on arcologies, self-sufficient habitats that could house whole cities, on Earth or on harsh worlds. It covers how such structures might work and what limits their size.
TqKQ94DtS54.why: HN commenters point to it in population and megacity discussions, mainly for its estimates of how many people arcologies could support and the heat, power and elevator bottlenecks.

TshYfYIxR9E.summary: Huygens Optics shows how DIY photon sieves shape a laser's wave front, explaining how they differ from zone plates and how aperture count affects the focal point, with time-resolved visualizations of the diffraction.
TshYfYIxR9E.why: HN points to it for a clear explanation of photon sieves versus Fresnel lenses and for showing what interference patterns actually look like.

T6JFTmQCFHg.summary: A 2004 short film adaptation of Terry Bisson's story "They're Made Out of Meat", in which aliens discuss the astonishing discovery of meat-based intelligent life. It stars Tom Noonan and Ben Bailey.
T6JFTmQCFHg.why: HN points to it as the best filmed version of the story whenever aliens or the nature of intelligence come up.

TM9h89Vo_Qo.summary: Bryan Cantrill's Scale By The Bay 2019 talk on software after Moore's Law. He covers the end of easy scaling and the move toward specialized, emerging architectures.
TM9h89Vo_Qo.why: HN recommends it as a history and analysis of the end of scaling from a well-regarded systems speaker, and lists it among the best talks of 2019.

TcEWRykSgwE.summary: A short clip of Jordan Peterson explaining Pareto distributions, using Soviet farm collectivization and the resulting famine as context. It also covers how outcomes concentrate in a few people.
TcEWRykSgwE.why: HN points to it for an accessible explanation of why wealth and creative output are so unevenly distributed.

Tml94je2edk.summary: Richard Feldman's GOTO Copenhagen 2022 talk on why dynamic languages like Python, Ruby, PHP and JavaScript rose in the 1990s and why each now has a popular static type checker. It argues that modern static typing recovers the advantages that made dynamic languages attractive.
Tml94je2edk.why: HN commenters cite it as a clear account of the trade-offs between static and dynamic typing and why the industry is swinging back to types.

TneLO5TdW_M.summary: Rick Reed of WhatsApp speaks at MeetBSD about running a messaging service on FreeBSD and Erlang at huge scale. He covers the stack, tuning and the challenges of millions of connections per host.
TneLO5TdW_M.why: Pointed to as a rare look at how a tiny engineering team ran WhatsApp's massive scale on FreeBSD and Erlang.

TrfD3pC0VSs.summary: Bryan Cantrill's illumos Day 2014 talk on running Linux containers on an illumos kernel via LX-branded zones. He covers emulating Linux syscalls on SmartOS and compares Linux and Solaris-derived systems.
TrfD3pC0VSs.why: HN points to it as an entertaining deep dive on Linux emulation on SmartOS and on how the Solaris kernel and libc are tightly coupled.

T-TwcmT6Rcw.summary: Raymond Hettinger explains Python's dataclasses module, showing the problem it solves and its key design decisions. He places it in a progression from tuples and dicts through named tuples and attrs.
T-TwcmT6Rcw.why: HN commenters recommend it as an approachable talk from a respected Python core developer on dataclasses.

T2IaJwkqgPk.summary: The full 2010 documentary Inside Job, directed by Charles Ferguson, examines the causes of the 2008 global financial crisis. It traces the story through interviews with key financial and political players across several countries.
T2IaJwkqgPk.why: HN points to it as an informative account of how the 2008 crisis developed and spread, and of conflicts of interest among economists and bankers.

TLm7Q92xMjQ.summary: Technology Connections explains how automatic windshield wiper rain sensors work, using an infrared light source and total internal reflection in the glass.
TLm7Q92xMjQ.why: Brought up in Tesla auto-wiper threads as the clear explanation of how simple conventional rain sensors work.

TMbl_ofF3AM.summary: A Channel 4 Equinox documentary on the NK-33 engines built for the Soviet N1 moon rocket and how they ended up in the USA. It includes rare footage and interviews with veterans of the early Soviet space program.
TMbl_ofF3AM.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating history of Soviet staged-combustion engines and why they stayed in use in American rockets.

TPuJsgyu87U.summary: Julia co-creator Jeff Bezanson candidly lists fundamental problems with the language at JuliaCon 2019, including modularity, types and compiler latency, and how they might be solved.
TPuJsgyu87U.why: HN cites it as the language creator's honest account of Julia's weaknesses, useful for anyone evaluating the language.

TRL7o2kPqw0.summary: Veritasium visits Chernobyl, Fukushima and other places to find who on Earth is exposed to the most ionizing radiation. The answer turns out to be surprising and puts radiation risk in context.
TRL7o2kPqw0.why: HN commenters use it to put radiation exposure and risk into perspective, including everyday sources like flights and smoking.

TTM_b7EJg5E.summary: Joe Armstrong, inventor of Erlang, gives a GOTO Chicago 2018 talk on building fault-tolerant systems. He covers what to do and avoid when handling errors, arguing for letting processes fail and recover.
TTM_b7EJg5E.why: Recommended as a conceptual rather than code-heavy talk on failure recovery from Erlang's creator.

TgFdics3uKo.summary: Rick Beato discusses a theory of why some children develop perfect pitch, based on early exposure to music. He draws on his experience with his own children.
TgFdics3uKo.why: Pointed to in threads on training absolute pitch in children as a practitioner's account.

Th4VlqQyVr4.summary: Thunderf00t analyzes the leaked Pentagon UFO videos and offers mundane explanations for the fuzzy triangle and tic-tac footage.
Th4VlqQyVr4.why: HN commenters point to it as a skeptical debunking of the Pentagon UFO videos.

ThjvMReOXYM.summary: Jon Gjengset's long live-coding Crust of Rust episode on async/await, focused on the mental model for using it rather than on Futures, Pin and Wakers internals. Topics include awaiting multiple futures, cancellation, executors and select.
ThjvMReOXYM.why: Recommended as a deep, practical dive for learning how Rust async works.

TiXINuf5nbI.summary: Jake Thackray performs the folk song Molly Metcalfe, which opens with an explanation of the traditional northern English sheep-counting system (yan, tan, tethera). It is a short, witty piece of British folk songwriting.
TiXINuf5nbI.why: HN recommends it in threads about sheep-counting systems as the famous song that explains them.

TlinocVHpzk.summary: Mentour Pilot, a 737 instructor, explains the approach-to-stall and escape manoeuvre and why the 737 MAX needs MCAS while the 737NG did not. He covers the jackscrew and pitch behavior in terms a general viewer can follow.
TlinocVHpzk.why: HN people recommend it as an easy-to-understand pilot's explanation of the 737 MAX MCAS issue.

TrC6ROeV4GI.summary: Hyrum Wright shares lessons from five years of mass code migrations in Google's huge C++ codebase. He covers why to migrate, how hard it really is, and how Google updates core libraries and their users continually.
TrC6ROeV4GI.why: HN points to it in monorepo and refactoring discussions as a great account of large-scale changes at Google.

TitZV6k8zfA.summary: Marques Brownlee reviews the Humane AI Pin and calls it the worst product he has reviewed, arguing almost no one should buy it. He explains why smartphones still beat it as a daily carry device.
TitZV6k8zfA.why: Referenced as the definitive review explaining why the AI Pin failed.

TjDEsGZLbio.summary: Tom Lehrer performs his satirical song about rocket scientist Wernher von Braun, with an introduction, in a short clip posted for the Apollo 11 anniversary. It lampoons von Braun's moral flexibility.
TjDEsGZLbio.why: HN brings it up as the sharpest satire of scientists who serve whoever pays them, and as a favorite Lehrer song.

T39QHprz-x8.summary: Al Baydha project co-founder Neal Spackman gives a final update nine years in, explaining how desertification followed the loss of indigenous land management and how the land has changed since inputs stopped in 2016. It lists which species worked best.
T39QHprz-x8.why: HN cites it as encouraging evidence that deserts can be regenerated and greened.

TAGjuRwx_Y8.summary: A travel vlogger asks the leader of the Hadza hunter-gatherers in Tanzania some big life questions just before a baboon hunt. The short answers touch on meat, honey and what matters in life.
TAGjuRwx_Y8.why: HN cites it as a glimpse of present-day hunter-gatherer life, for example on diet and teeth, though one commenter calls it flippant and sensationalist.

TEBMlXRjhZY.summary: Ashley Feniello demonstrates VimSpeak, a voice-controlled interface for Vim inspired by Tavis Rudd's voice programming talk. The demo includes working through a VimGolf challenge by speech.
TEBMlXRjhZY.why: HN mentions it as an example of voice-driven editing, and one commenter says it clarified how Vim commands compose.

TJYOkZz6Dck.summary: An English-subtitled version of Staplerfahrer Klaus, a gory dark-comedy German workplace safety film about the dangers of forklifts in warehouses.
TJYOkZz6Dck.why: Brought up as a beloved classic whenever forklifts or workplace safety come up in a thread.

TM8L7bdwVaA.summary: A Conan segment compiling local news anchors who all read the same scripted copy during the holiday season. It highlights how homogenized local broadcast news has become.
TM8L7bdwVaA.why: Used as the go-to illustration of corporate-owned local newscasts reading identical scripts.

TMoz3gSXBcY.summary: Physicist Angela Collier critiques 'vibe physics', the idea that non-experts or billionaires can make scientific discoveries by chatting with AI chatbots, drawing a parallel with vibe coding.
TMoz3gSXBcY.why: HN points to it as a takedown of AI-assisted amateur physics, though a few commenters push back on it.

TS1lpKBMkgg.summary: Paul Phillips, a former Scala core contributor, argues after moving a million lines of code that much of what the software industry does is wrong. He critiques Scala and compiler design and calls for better approaches.
TS1lpKBMkgg.why: Cited as an insider's critique of Scala and of non-incremental compilers, often by people warning others off Scala.

TSZMtSPX3iE.summary: A two-minute remix-style video set to Hall of the Mountain King that mocks Anthony Fauci's Covid pandemic statements. It circulated widely among vaccine and mandate skeptics.
TSZMtSPX3iE.why: Cited as an example of the viral anti-establishment Covid videos shared in those circles, rather than as a recommendation.

TaU1UH_3B5k.summary: City Beautiful explains how Houston, which has no formal zoning, still shapes land use through deed restrictions, parking minimums and buffering ordinances.
TaU1UH_3B5k.why: HN uses it as the standard primer for the point that Houston's 'no zoning' is a misconception, since its rules produce similar effects.

Tct38KwROdw.summary: A Vox reporter tries to learn what his son's birth would cost before it happens and fails, showing how opaque US hospital pricing is even for the most common procedure.
Tct38KwROdw.why: HN cites it as the go-to example of how impossible it is to get prices in advance for US medical care.

Tl9kD693ie4.summary: Jensen Harris of the Office 2007 design team tells the behind-the-scenes story of the Ribbon at MIX08. He covers early prototypes, mistakes, and the UX principles used to design and validate it.
Tl9kD693ie4.why: HN points to it to explain the design rationale behind the Ribbon and why the older menu and toolbar interface had accumulated too much cruft.

TlO2gcs1YvM.summary: A dramatized fictional video of micro drones with facial recognition and swarm AI used as autonomous killer weapons. It is a Slaughterbots-style warning about lethal autonomous weapons.
TlO2gcs1YvM.why: Linked in drone and military AI threads as a chilling dramatization, though some find it alarmist.

Tn7egDQ9lPg.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on organ and body donation, covering where donations actually go, how donated bodies are used and sold, and problems in organ transplant programs.
Tn7egDQ9lPg.why: HN cites it in threads about donated bodies and organ transplant failures as a critical look at opaque systems.

TnzcwTyr6cE.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation on using gene drives to modify mosquitoes against malaria, and whether we should. It explains the mechanism and the ethical trade-offs.
TnzcwTyr6cE.why: HN links it as a clear explainer of gene drive when mosquito genetic engineering comes up.

ToKcmnrE5oY.summary: A Mitchell and Webb sketch in which two German soldiers realize their uniforms carry skulls and wonder whether they are the baddies. It is a short comedy bit about people failing to see themselves as the villains.
ToKcmnrE5oY.why: Cited constantly as a quip when a person or organization seems to be doing something morally dubious.

TptzkkbC1vE.summary: Carwow's review of the McMurtry Spéirling, a 1,000hp electric fan car that generates huge downforce at standstill and reaches 0-60mph in about 1.4 seconds.
TptzkkbC1vE.why: HN cites it as the example of an extremely fast production electric car that uses ground suction fans.

TBb9O-aW4zI.summary: A satirical CBC Radio This Is That sketch profiling a Vancouver artisanal firewood company that sells bundles of kindling for $1000.
TBb9O-aW4zI.why: HN uses it as a punchline reference when a product or trend seems like a parody of artisanal premium goods.

TCbFEgFajGU.summary: A 2007 clip in which immigration attorneys describe how they help employers run classified ads designed not to find qualified American applicants, so they can secure green cards for H-1B workers. It is presented as an exposé of the PERM process.
TCbFEgFajGU.why: HN commenters in H-1B debates post it as evidence that the labor-market test is gamed with fake job ads.

TDkH3EbWTYc.summary: LabCoatz uses mass spectrometry, with help from other science YouTubers, to reverse engineer the Coca-Cola flavor and builds a chemically-identical replica. The video walks through a year of work on the formula.
TDkH3EbWTYc.why: HN mostly cites it as a notable example of reverse engineering a famously secret formula, not as a recommendation.

TF8THY5spmo.summary: A time-lapse from ESO's Very Large Telescope showing stars orbiting the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center over nearly 20 years.
TF8THY5spmo.why: HN links it as direct observational evidence for a massive invisible object at the galactic center.

TFEvkmvIjVo.summary: AutoX shows its fully driverless robotaxi navigating dense, chaotic urban village streets in Chinese cities. The vehicle nudges through crowds, bikes, scooters and pets.
TFEvkmvIjVo.why: Cited as evidence that Chinese robotaxis handle difficult edge cases in self-driving debates.

TGD8zKvRxc4.summary: A step-by-step tutorial on making a Harry Potter by Balenciaga style AI video, using tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney and Eleven Labs for script, images and voices.
TGD8zKvRxc4.why: HN cites it as a process example of how such AI-generated videos are made, including on a phone.

TGfQu0bQTKc.summary: A short comedy sketch by Kai Lentit lampooning an interview with a 'senior Rust developer' and Rust community stereotypes.
TGfQu0bQTKc.why: HN posts it as a humorous aside in Rust debates, often to poke fun at Rust evangelism and community culture.

TGkPMZxWPpA.summary: A Dutch parody commercial from the Groen Brothers for a supposed Star Wars style mosquito defense system. It mimics the style of infomercials with laser-armed anti-mosquito technology.
TGkPMZxWPpA.why: Brought up as a joke or tongue-in-cheek prior art whenever someone proposes shooting insects or pests with lasers.

THNPmhBl-8I.summary: A short That Mitchell and Webb Look sketch in which a rocket scientist and a brain surgeon trade jibes over whose job is harder. It is a BBC comedy clip from 2009.
THNPmhBl-8I.why: Mostly posted as a joke or reference when threads touch on status, difficulty or jobs.

TIClA57jWmQ.summary: Footage of CNN reporter Omar Jimenez and his crew being arrested live on air while covering the Minneapolis protests after the killing of George Floyd. He identified himself as press and offered to move.
TIClA57jWmQ.why: HN cites it as evidence in discussions of police treatment of journalists at protests.

TIClAanU7Os.summary: A short clip from Macworld 1999 in which actor Noah Wyle, who played Steve Jobs in Pirates of Silicon Valley, appears on stage as Jobs at the start of the keynote. Jobs then joins in.
TIClAanU7Os.why: HN cites it as a funny piece of Apple history and as evidence of Jobs's showmanship and good humor about his portrayal.

TJgUiZgX5rE.summary: Footage of IIHS tests of pedestrian automatic emergency braking on 16 midsize cars, with ratings from superior to basic or no credit.
TJgUiZgX5rE.why: HN references it as evidence that pedestrian-detecting emergency braking is routinely tested by independent agencies.

TMuno5RZNeE.summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) gives a talk on the SOLID principles of object-oriented and agile design, in the context of encapsulation and clean code.
TMuno5RZNeE.why: Cited in discussions of OO design, access modifiers and private fields, and why writing messy code slows you down.

TP9kokeyxGU.summary: Fully Charged gets an exclusive first drive of the Porsche Taycan, running 0-200 km/h launch control repeatedly. It covers the car's twin-motor 800-volt specs, claimed range and fast charging.
TP9kokeyxGU.why: Used in Tesla comparison threads to show the Taycan repeating launches without overheating or losing performance.

TUS0Zv2APjU.summary: LGR reviews the Danmere Backer16, a 1996 backup system that stored a PC's data on ordinary VHS tapes through a VCR. He shows the hardware and software on Windows 3.1 and 95.
TUS0Zv2APjU.why: HN links it whenever data-on-video-tape or YouTube-as-storage schemes come up, as the real precedent for storing digital data on VHS.

TWFzWRoVNnE.summary: Linus Tech Tips' rant on Intel's X299 platform and Core i9 launch, criticizing how Intel segments the market by limiting PCIe lanes and charging for features like VROC keys.
TWFzWRoVNnE.why: HN cites it as a source for Intel's market-segmentation tactics on its high-end desktop platform.

TY4s35uULg4.summary: Linus Tech Tips tests a Chinese mining-only Nvidia card, hacked with a modified driver so it can render games and output video through an integrated GPU.
TY4s35uULg4.why: HN cites it as precedent for repurposing mining-only GPUs for graphics, in threads about Nvidia limiting mining on gaming cards.

TbHBHhZOglw.summary: Technology Connections explains how touch lamps work and traces them back through patents to the 1950s, far earlier than most people assume.
TbHBHhZOglw.why: HN uses it as an example of Google's search answers confidently giving the wrong date for the invention.

TbwlC2B-BIg.summary: An SNL sketch in which Adam Sandler plays a tour operator who bluntly clarifies what his Italy tours can and cannot do for customers' lives.
TbwlC2B-BIg.why: Used as a funny reference for realistic expectations about travel and whether it fixes your life.

TijcoS8qHIE.summary: A one-minute Canadian public-service spot about a house hippo, a hoax that makes the point that you should not believe everything you see on television.
TijcoS8qHIE.why: Used as a joking reference when threads discuss fake news, hoaxes and gullibility.

Tj-KS2kfIr0.summary: A 2007 video review of the Neonode N1m phone, which uses touch gestures including a swipe to unlock. It was published just before the iPhone's launch.
Tj-KS2kfIr0.why: Used as evidence of prior art for slide-to-unlock in patent disputes involving Apple.

TkX-TPaodoM.summary: A clip from the film Up in the Air in which George Clooney's character fires a man and urges him to return to the dreams of his youth. The movie features real people reacting to being laid off.
TkX-TPaodoM.why: Referenced in threads about layoffs and career choices for its depiction of firing and giving up on dreams.

TlJob8K_OwE.summary: A Google Developers Q&A in which Blink engineering leads and the PM answer the community's top questions about the new Blink rendering engine forked from WebKit.
TlJob8K_OwE.why: HN cited it for direct statements from the Chrome team about the WebKit split, Dart integration and Blink's direction.

Tmx1jpqv3RA.summary: A short Simpsons clip in which Homer distinguishes between jealousy and envy.
Tmx1jpqv3RA.why: Only used as a joke when threads about envy or jealousy come up.

TqAu-DDlINs.summary: A Burnistoun sketch in which a voice-recognition elevator cannot understand two Scottish men saying the number eleven. It satirizes voice interfaces that fail on accents.
TqAu-DDlINs.why: HN invokes it as the go-to joke whenever voice interfaces, speech recognition or natural-language UIs are discussed.

TsNc4nEX3c4.summary: Guardian News clip of Elon Musk announcing the 'Tesla Bot' at AI Day 2021, with a person dancing in a bodysuit on stage in place of a prototype.
TsNc4nEX3c4.why: HN invokes it as a joke about Tesla's overpromised robotics and AI claims.

TsdOej_nC1M.summary: A short look at the Voder, the first electronic voice synthesizer, demonstrated by Bell Labs at the 1939 World's Fair. It was operated by trained women using ten finger keys, foot pedals and a knee lever.
TsdOej_nC1M.why: HN cites it as a historic demonstration of early speech synthesis, including discussions about whether the demo was genuine.

TtmLVP0HvDg.summary: A one-minute clip of the New Caledonian crow Betty bending a straight wire into a hook to retrieve food from a tube. It comes from a 2002 Science study on tool-making in crows.
TtmLVP0HvDg.why: HN links it as the clearest demonstration that crows can fashion tools.

TuupoxmeQ6U.summary: A short video of someone playing Doom on a TI-83+ graphing calculator, with a link to the version used.
TuupoxmeQ6U.why: Cited as the best available video of Doom on a TI calculator in threads about Doom ports and calculator programming.

TzcJlKg2Rc0.summary: A 2019 extended interview in which Connie Loizos talks with Sam Altman about his work, OpenAI's capped-profit structure, its mission toward safe artificial general intelligence, and criticisms the organization faces.
TzcJlKg2Rc0.why: It is mostly cited critically or jokingly, as a source for Altman's early statements about AGI and investor promises that commenters later quote back at him.
